Name: target_cluster_downsample_budget
Title: Target-Cluster Budget: cap=0 with Fair Matched Control
Experiment: Six-condition protocol: cap=0; matched_random_embedding samples N=embedding target cluster; matched_random_linguistic samples N=linguistic target cluster; all_mixed uses full pool (ceiling). Verify clustering beats its paired matched control on low_resource_macro_f1 / average_f1.

Name: head_final_cohesion
Title: Constrained Clustering: Keep ja-ko-mn Together for East-Asian Transfer
Experiment: Modify cluster_embedding() so ja, ko, mn must share one cluster (hard or soft constraint) before/during agglomerative clustering. Cap500 floor: embedding groups {ja,ko,mn} but still loses to matched_random on pool transfer. Add cohesion constraint. Success: embedding_clustering beats matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1; mn F1 is secondary evidence.

Name: script_aware_mn_ru_penalty
Title: Script-Aware Typology Distance: Penalize Cyrillic Script Confusion
Experiment: Extend _hybrid_lang_distance_matrix() with an extra penalty when pairing typologically distant languages that share script (e.g. mn-ru). Goal: improve cluster purity and pool-wide transfer, not mn-only tuning. Tune penalty weight. Compare embedding vs matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and per-language F1.

Name: typology_weighted_mixture
Title: Soft Typology-Weighted Training Mixture Instead of Hard Cluster Cut
Experiment: Replace hard langs_in_cluster() selection with typology-based language weights across the pool. Sample or weight training sentences proportional to typology similarity to each eval language (or cluster centroid). Still report as embedding_clustering regime. Target: beat matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and pool macro F1.

Name: k2_silhouette_head_final
Title: Silhouette k Selection with k>=2 and HEAD_FINAL Merger
Experiment: Change _select_k_by_silhouette() to search k in {2,3,4} with optional typology-prior merge so related East-Asian languages co-locate. Addresses pathological splits without abandoning data-driven k. Evaluate pool-wide transfer vs matched_random.

Name: low_resource_reweight
Title: Low-Resource Stratum Reweighting in Transfer Mixtures
Experiment: Implement augment_train_raw(): up-weight sentences from low_resource_macro_f1 stratum languages within selected transfer languages (not mn-only). Improves low-resource transfer without changing cluster assignment logic. Success: low_resource_macro_f1 > matched_random.

Name: typology_guided_diversity_expansion
Title: Typology-Guided Diversity Expansion: Using Linguistic Distance to Grow, Not Shrink, the Training Pool
Experiment:
IMPORTANT: cluster_embedding()'s output is NOT deterministic across runs, so do NOT rely on calling cluster_linguistic()/cluster_embedding() to reproduce the floor's base cluster. Instead, hardcode the base cluster directly: BASE_CLUSTER = ['ja', 'ko', 'mn'] (do not call cluster_embedding()/cluster_linguistic() to derive it, and do not modify those functions). Use BASE_CLUSTER as train_langs for both embedding_clustering and linguistic_clustering in post_cluster_train_langs().

Implement diversity via REPLACEMENT in augment_train_raw(raw_ds, train_langs, cfg, condition_name), following this EXACT procedure (do not use direct item assignment on a Dataset object -- datasets.Dataset does NOT support raw_ds[i] = ...; it is immutable and must be rebuilt via select()/concatenate_datasets()):
1. other_langs = [l for l in LANGUAGES if l not in train_langs] (the 29-lang pool minus the base cluster).
2. candidate_ds = load_raw_ner_dataset(other_langs, 'train', cfg) -- load this as a SEPARATE dataset object, do not reuse raw_ds's own indices as the candidate pool.
3. n_replace = int(len(raw_ds) * replacement_ratio).
4. Use a local numpy RandomState seeded from cfg.seed to pick n_replace indices to DROP from raw_ds, and n_replace indices to SAMPLE from candidate_ds.
5. keep_indices = sorted(set(range(len(raw_ds))) - set(dropped_indices)); base_remaining = raw_ds.select(keep_indices).
6. sampled_candidates = candidate_ds.select(sampled_candidate_indices).
7. new_ds = datasets.concatenate_datasets([base_remaining, sampled_candidates]) and return new_ds. Do not mutate raw_ds in place anywhere.
8. assert len(new_ds) == len(raw_ds), 'replacement must preserve total N' -- raise if this fails rather than silently returning a mismatched dataset.

Sweep the replacement ratio R (= replacement_ratio) across the 5 runs: monotonically increasing, no repeated value, spanning from near-0% to near-100%, at least 4 distinct values (e.g. R roughly 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%). Use SOURCE-SPECIFIC ranking when choosing which candidate languages to sample from candidate_ds (not which individual sentences, language-level is sufficient): for source='linguistic', prefer languages closer by pure linguistic/typological distance (URIEL/lang2vec features only, no embeddings) to BASE_CLUSTER; for source='embedding', prefer languages closer by pure sentence-embedding distance (no typology penalty term) to BASE_CLUSTER's centroid. Before reporting any run, assert final n_train_samples equals matched_random's N=40100; if they differ, treat the run as invalid and fix the code rather than reporting it. Verify before each run that its R value and resulting language distribution differ from every previous run. Success: embedding_clustering and/or linguistic_clustering (with replacement) beats matched_random on low_resource_macro_f1 and/or average_f1 at some value of R, at equal N throughout.
